builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
summary: The framework replaces informal prompt-sensitivity checks for LLM-based social simulation agents with systematic context-enrichment substitution rules (neutral padding, social background, descriptive and normative grounding) evaluated against a selective robustness criterion: invariance to meaning-preserving prompt changes plus directional sensitivity to decision-relevant changes. Cost is additional prompt engineering and multiplied evaluation runs across variants and models; it uses existing API or single-GPU inference, so no new infrastructure is required, but the token cost of enriched contexts rises with prompt length. Results are model-dependent—the two tested models showed distinct behavioral patterns—so enrichment choices validated on one model may not transfer, and findings demonstrated in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game may not generalize to other simulation settings.
rationale: The validation criterion is directly usable with API-only infrastructure and addresses a real production risk (prompt brittleness), but the absence of quantified gains and the model-dependent results require workload-specific testing before adoption.
technique: Controlled context enrichment with selective robustness validation
